title: My cockle hat and staff and hismy sandal shoon.
html_source:
Ophelia’s song from ‘Hamlet’:

How should I your true-love know,
From another one?
By his cockle hat and staff,
And his sandal shoon.

Given that Stephen draws artistic inspiration from Hamlet, he may believe that he needs to find love before artistic inspiration. A possibility that is supported previously in this Chapter:

“Touch me. Soft eyes. Soft soft soft hand. I am lonely here. O, touch me soon, now. What is that word known to all men? I am quiet here alone. Sad too. Touch, touch me”

anchor.suffix:
Where? To evening lands. Evening will find itself. 

 He took the hilt of his ashplant, lunging with it softly, dallying still. Yes, evening will find itself in me, without me. Al
